reason: Start with the kidney's filtering structure, where blood enters the nephron.
expectation: The capillary tufts should fit inside the capsules to form a filtration unit; I expect details of what crosses the filter.

alternatives.reason: The tubules are needed for recovery, but filtration seems a natural place to start.

effect: The filter passes useful substances as well as waste, so the recovery tubules are the next priority.
reaction: The need to reclaim glucose and water makes the filter's limitations clear.
reason: Add selective transport proteins to the tubules to prepare a recovery route.
expectation: The tubules will gain transport mechanisms for reclaiming substances from filtered fluid; how they connect to blood remains to be seen.

effect: The tubules now have selective transport proteins; connecting them to the filter should establish the fluid's recovery path.
reaction: The distinction between solute transport and water following osmotic gradients is useful.
reason: Connect the filtering units to the recovery tubules so filtered fluid can enter them.
expectation: The capsule outlets will join the tubules, forming a continuous filtration and recovery route; blood-vessel connections may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: Blood vessels are also needed for recovery, but connecting the fluid pathway first seems natural.

effect: The filter and tubule now form a nephron, but the recovery route still needs its blood vessels.
reaction: The separate tubular and capillary spaces make the arrangement clear.
reason: Connect the working units to blood vessels to establish the supply and recovery pathway.
expectation: Blood vessels will connect to the filters and surround the tubules, allowing reclaimed substances to return to blood.

effect: The nephron units now have a continuous blood supply and vessels around the recovery tubules; the urine drainage route remains to be built.
reaction: The vessels continuing from the filter to the tubules make the return pathway easier to follow.
reason: Connect the collecting ducts to the kidney drainage funnels to build the next part of the urine pathway.
expectation: The ducts will merge into the calyces and renal pelvis, ready to connect to the ureters.

alternatives.reason: The ureters and bladder also need connecting, but I chose to build outward from the kidney first.

effect: The collecting ducts now lead through calyces to a renal pelvis, ready to join the working kidney units.
reaction: The open ureter outlet makes the remaining drainage route clear.
reason: Connect the nephron units to the collecting trees to complete the kidney's internal fluid pathway.
expectation: The tubules will drain into collecting ducts, joining filtration and recovery to the renal pelvis.

alternatives.reason: The ureters and bladder also need connecting, but I want to finish the kidney pathway first.

effect: The kidneys now join filtration and recovery to collecting ducts while keeping blood and urine pathways distinct.
reaction: The parallel routes make it clear where reclaimed material and remaining fluid go.
reason: Connect the kidneys to the ureters to extend the urine pathway outward.
expectation: The renal pelvis of each kidney will connect to a ureter, leaving a route to the bladder still to complete.

alternatives.reason: The bladder and urethra also need the ureters, but connecting outward from the kidneys follows the fluid path.
